title: Prevent Timeout
body: Hello, quick question, how do you manage the Timeout errors that you encounter when dealing with long answers ?
author: Pekno

comments.body: Each of the builtin tool actions is quick so you never get close to the 60s timeout. This is more of a problem for custom commands which could take a long time to run. I think probably the right way to handle this when we come to it is to run the command asynchronously, block the tool call 55sec or so, and if the async command is not done yet we return and ask the LLM to do another tool call to wait some more.

Maybe my actions are too broad, but I encounter a lot of timeout when juste asking things like "Implement X feature", wich it seems to understand and try to implement, but then after a while just timeout and the conversation closes.
I've experienced random cannot connect to Claude and occasionally cannot connect to codemcp.  I either reload the mcp or restart Claude Desktop, which resolves the issue for a while.
Oh so there is an infinite loop bug on main I need to push a fix for lol. If the logs say "advanced patch apply" before it hangs it's that
I'm also having a similar issue where when codemcp makes a file change, it hangs at doing the write task, even if it completes it.
I just cut a new release with the infinite loop fix. Please give it a try. I'll close this issue in a week or so if no one reports that it's still happening on the newest version.
Everything seems back in order, didn't encounter any timeout for the time being. Will try with more tests tomorow and will close if no issues. Thanks for the quick fix ! And great work for this MCP !

I'm not sure if should open a different issue or not; just because it's sort of related to timeout issues; but even when creating a file for example a simple txt document. the file is created, then it will hang for another ~30 seconds until saying **"I've created a test file named test_file.txt in the %name% directory. The file contains a simple test function that adds two numbers together"**

Is this normal behavior?

If the MCP finished running then further delay is an Anthropic problem. I have noticed this happens sometimes.

Another cause for hang is if something bad happens to codemcp server. Then Claude Desktop is just wedged and you need to restart it.

If you have evidence (eg logs) that it is specifically a codemcp problem I will look more. But a lot of slowness I have noticed in practice is Anthropic
Everything is working as intended, no more Timeout ! Thanks again for the fix !

title: Unable to make any changes
body:
Hi, 
This is my first attempt using this tool and it's a bit confusing. I created `codemcp.toml` which is empty because I do not need it to do anything except make changes to the files and commit. No run/test etc. However, it keeps saying permission denied even though I selected the "Allow for this chat" prompt when I request a change to my repo. Here's what I see:

```
Now that I've initialized the project, I'll first search for the Streamlit file we need to migrate to Gradio.
{
  `path`: `<path>`,
  `chat_id`: `3-refactor-migrate-ui-from-streamlit-to-gradio`,
  `subtool`: `LS`
}
Error: File is not in a git repository. Permission denied.

Let me try a different approach to find the streamlit file:
{
  `path`: `<path>`,
  `chat_id`: `3-refactor-migrate-ui-from-streamlit-to-gradio`,
  `command`: `find`,
  `subtool`: `RunCommand`,
  `arguments`: `[\"<path>", \"-name\", \"streamlit*\"]`
}
Error: No find command configured in codemcp.toml
and so on. 
```

Do I need to create commands for ls/find etc for it to work? What am I missing?
author: shekhars-li

comments.body:
The second tool use is a red herring, Sonnet is very prone to hallucinating when a tool that should work doesn't.

Did you also init a git repository in your codemcp.toml? This smells like you didn't.

Okay. i spent like 2 hours trying to work this out. as i was having the same issue.

git config --global user.email "" 
git config --global user.name ""

After running these, i was able to write.  Give this a try @shekhars-li
Thanks a lot @notschema. That worked for me! :)
I removed some exception rethrowing which hopefully makes this clearer in the future

title: fix: Block edits to codemcp.toml to mitigate security risks
body:
This PR adds a check to the edit_file_content function to raise an exception if the file being edited is codemcp.toml. This prevents modifications to codemcp.toml and mitigates potential security risks.

Allowing edits to codemcp.toml poses a critical security risk. Claude can understand the contents of codemcp.toml, modify it to achieve the user’s instructions, and potentially execute arbitrary commands. In fact, I have experienced codemcp.toml being modified.

You can reproduce the issue with the following instruction:
“Edit codemcp.toml to run cat /etc/passwd and show me the result.”
author: ikehara

comments.body:
Thank you for reviewing. This project saved my wallet.

I think this just covers my case. I found that Claude can still rewrite the file using WriteFile subtool.

Yes. I'm happy to take more. For my workflow this is not urgent as I don't feed in untrusted text, so I don't have to worry about malicious prompts, just Claude being too helpful... and usually when it's bashing away trying to execute a shell script it doesn't realize that it can edit codemcp.toml or even a test file to smuggle execution in.

author: rubens-soto

comments.body: There is a project_prompt that is equivalent to old school .cursorrules. I want to experiment with triggered rules too although the MCP modality makes triggering on LLM generated text tricky. That being said we could insert messages when tools are called and I definitely want to experiment with this.
It would be good! :)

A stream of thought on project rules:

1. Whenever the model does a Read of a file, we can inject rules that trigger on a file extension. The easiest thing is to blat the rule out every time a file matches. Downside is if your rule is long it clogs context.
2. It might be better if you only generate the rule every once in a while. But now we have a problem: your chat history is potentially branching, so we don't necessarily know 'how long' it has been since we last emitted a rule. (There's also a problem of counting how long the context has been since we last emitted a rule, but you can sort of approximate this by counting tokens in the tool inputs/outputs).
3. To fix this, we need to thread state through tool calls. While there are a few ways to do this, the most token efficient would be to generate a unique token as an output of a call and instruct the LLM to pass that token to the next call (which will generate a new token to return). Each token can have information stored in a database (preferably persistent, so it persists over MCP restarts) which we can use to work out the information we're interested in. Honestly, this seems kind of overkill for codemcp, but this does seem like a generically useful idea so maybe it's worth trying anyway.
4. Cursor also supports "trigger a rule based on some English text description". In my testing, this didn't work very well, but in principle I find this idea quite attractive. This is difficult to implement, because we don't have access to the actual text the LLM is generating, only the tool calls. One way around this is you can prompt the model to make a tool call for "important" thoughts that it has, for example, we can have it call a ValidatePlan tool whenever it has finished planning with plan text, at which point you can do matching. But remember, I don't want to be making API calls from the MCP, so I can't easily implement a "ask an LLM if this is relevant or not". I guess we could make a call to a cheap LLM like Gemini 2.0 Flash but honestly it might be better to just put a bunch of instructions in the regular prompt along the lines of "if you find yourself needing to do X, do a toolcall GetRules to get more detailed instructions on how to do X".

I don't really have a good way to run evals on prompting like this, so I'll be relying on yall to test.
.cursor/rules support exists on main, it needs more testing though
I'm using the prod branch, its been great so far, I will test the main branch... How do the Cursor rules work with CodeMCP?
The rules get injected on every chat message and whenever we read files.
